author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has been MIA since its 2024 reveal at The Game Awards, but developer Naughty Dog says that will change next year. The game will get a full reveal—and maybe even a release date—sometime in 2027, and studio head Neil Druckmann asked for fans' patience while the devs 'cook for just a little bit longer.' In other news, former PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida thinks Sony and Nintendo need to hang onto the the current generation of consoles for as long as they can. Skyrocketing electronics component prices will likely put any new console out of reach for a lot of gamers, and there seems to be no rush to move on from the troubled PS5 and Nintendo Switch 2 generation. And finally, Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie adaptation was such a big hit, it boosted sales of some of the older game titles. Resident Evils 2 and 4 saw a 50% spike in sales on the PS5, no doubt also helped by a recent sale on those games.
title: Naughty Dog Has Two 'The Last of Us' Projects In the Works - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
What makes a video game choice stick with you long after the credits roll? Step into the war-torn landscape of Velen as we unpack "The Bloody Baron": widely celebrated as one of the greatest quests in modern RPG history. Far beyond a simple monster hunt in Geralt’s search for Ciri, this dark fantasy story arc forces players to navigate trauma, morality, and the illusion of control as they uncover the tragic, layered past of one Phillip Strenger, the titular warlord, and his estranged family. Featuring direct design commentary from CD Projekt Red's Paweł Sasko, the quest's original designer, this deep dive explores how gameplay mechanics, detective work, and deliberate narrative subversion merge to create an unforgettable masterclass in video game storytelling.

In this comprehensive quest analysis of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, we break down the narrative structure, level design, and branching choices behind the Bloody Baron tetralogy. From Geralt’s Witcher Senses crime scene investigat
title: The Witcher 3 Quest That Nobody Forgets: The Bloody Baron | Art of the Level

author: IGN
description:
Godzilla movies have long had a problem: What do you do after the initial thrill of a quote/unquote _serious _Godzilla origin story? Can the filmmakers somehow continue the deep thematic underpinnings of that first adventure, even while upping the visual ante with more giant monster action? How do you offer a probing commentary about the world we live in – which is what the best of the genre is known for – when you’ve got skyscraper-sized lizards slugging it out MMA-style?

It is under these circumstances – or should I say restrictions? – that [Godzilla Minus Zero](https://www.ign.com/articles/godzilla-minus-zero-review) enters the ring. As the sequel to the much-praised [Godzilla Minus One](https://www.ign.com/articles/godzilla-minus-one-review) from three years ago – a picture that dealt with, among other things, notions of survivor’s guilt, hope in the face of hopelessness, found family, and more – Minus Zero is on the ropes from the start. Can returning writer-director Takashi Yam
title: Godzilla Minus Zero Review
